## Motivation

KDA chunked prefill currently materializes the recurrent state for every 64-token chunk and the corrected value tensor in `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`, then reads both back in `chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk`. For GLM-5.3-Flash prefill on gfx950 this creates an avoidable HBM round trip between the state recurrence and output calculation.

This change adds an opt-in gfx950 chain kernel that keeps each FP32 `[BV, K]` recurrent-state slice on chip while walking all chunks and produces the output in the same launch.

## Modifications

- Add a gfx950 Triton KDA chain kernel for BF16 Q/K/V/W/A, FP32 per-channel gates, `K=V=128`, and varlen batches.
- Keep recurrent state in FP32 across the chunk walk; write only the output, optional FP32 tracking snapshot, and final state.
- Preserve `-1` state-index semantics, envelope-strided state pools, partial tail chunks, deterministic accumulation, and CUDA-graph replay.
- Add the default-off `SGLANG_OPT_KDA_CHAIN_PREFILL` selector.
- Restrict dispatch to measured 16,384-token cells:
  - TP4 geometry: 16 local heads and 3 sequences.
  - TP8 geometry: 8 local heads and 2, 3, or 4 sequences.
- Preserve the existing state/output path for every unsupported or unmeasured dtype, shape, layout, hardware, tracking contract, and selector state.
- Add registered gfx950 correctness tests and a multi-sequence benchmark.

Enable with:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_KDA_CHAIN_PREFILL=1
```

## Accuracy Tests

On MI355X/gfx950, 22 focused tests passed. Coverage includes TP4/TP8 head geometries, ragged boundaries at 1/63/64/65/127 tokens, long 4×4,096-token inputs, multiple sequences, `-1` state indices, envelope-strided state storage, zero/nonzero state evolution, FP32 tracking snapshots, finite outputs, deterministic replay, CUDA-graph replay, and dispatch fallbacks.

The fused output matches the existing two-kernel path within one BF16 output quantum (`atol=6.2e-5`, `rtol=8e-3`); final BF16 recurrent state is bit-exact. Tracking snapshots retain the FP32 accumulator and round bit-exactly to the existing BF16 chunk-boundary state.


Full GLM-5.3-Flash GSM8K on the MXFP4 snapshot `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`, thinking enabled, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, sampling seed unset:

| TP | Configuration | Examples | Threads | Max output tokens | Score | Stop rate | Truncated rate | Error rate |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | Existing state/output pair | 1,319 | 64 | 32,768 | 97.12% | 100.00% | 0.00% | 0.00% |
| 4 | Chain selector enabled | 1,319 | 64 | 32,768 | 97.04% | 99.92% | 0.08% | 0.00% |
| 8 | Existing state/output pair | 1,319 | 1,200 | 4,096 | 96.82% | 99.39% | 0.61% | 0.00% |
| 8 | Chain selector enabled | 1,319 | 1,200 | 4,096 | 96.82% | 99.70% | 0.30% | 0.00% |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment:

- Hardware: AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`)
- Docker image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261013`
- Source: integration snapshot `0f5bab5cc7` (feature head `9c5b62e7df`)
- AITER: `e7d2453f25` with the image checkout's existing local modifications
- Workload: synthetic contiguous BF16 Q/K/V/W/A, FP32 gate, `K=V=128`, BT=64, 16,384 total tokens
- Timing: device events, 3 warmups, median of 20 measured repetitions; state and value inputs reset outside the timed region

### KDA state/output chain latency

The baseline is `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` followed by `chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk`. The candidate is `chunk_kda_chain_fwd`.

| Local heads | Sequences | Existing pair (ms) | Chain (ms) | Delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 3 | 0.3355 | 0.3163 | **-5.73%** |
| 8 | 2 | 0.3724 | 0.2920 | **-21.59%** |
| 8 | 3 | 0.2774 | 0.2439 | **-12.08%** |
| 8 | 4 | 0.2355 | 0.2024 | **-14.07%** |

Every enabled cell beats the existing pair. All other cells retain the fallback.


### End-to-end serving

GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 snapshot `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`, TP4, random 8,192-token input / 1,024-token output. The first concurrency-4 run in each repetition is the warmup; the tables average exactly the two measured runs per concurrency. Both arms use integration source `69cd329e57`, image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261014`, and the same shared warmed AITER/Triton caches; they differ only by `SGLANG_OPT_KDA_CHAIN_PREFILL`.

A. Existing state/output pair — selector disabled:

| Concurrency | TTFT (ms) | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) | Output tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 521.34 | 6.650 | 7323.26 | 559.09 |
| 8 | 834.89 | 7.810 | 8823.93 | 928.03 |
| 16 | 1423.75 | 9.555 | 11197.59 | 1462.60 |
| 32 | 2582.05 | 12.365 | 15232.97 | 2150.34 |
| 64 | 4904.58 | 16.710 | 22001.64 | 2977.56 |

B. Chain selector enabled (delta versus A):

| Concurrency | TTFT (ms) | Delta | ITL (ms) | Delta | E2EL (ms) | Delta | Output tok/s | Delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 520.95 | -0.07% | 6.640 | -0.15% | 7317.42 | -0.08% | 559.52 | +0.08% |
| 8 | 834.31 | -0.07% | 7.820 | +0.13% | 8830.00 | +0.07% | 927.37 | -0.07% |
| 16 | 1424.85 | +0.08% | 9.565 | +0.10% | 11208.96 | +0.10% | 1461.13 | -0.10% |
| 32 | 2585.13 | +0.12% | 12.380 | +0.12% | 15252.27 | +0.13% | 2147.56 | -0.13% |
| 64 | 4911.99 | +0.15% | 16.720 | +0.06% | 22017.27 | +0.07% | 2975.40 | -0.07% |

TP4 end-to-end results are neutral within approximately ±0.15%; the isolated kernel improvement does not produce a consistent serving gain.

### TP8 end-to-end serving

The TP8 recipe uses 131,072 context, all eight MI355X GPUs, and the same random 8K/1K workload and repetition policy.

A. Existing state/output pair — selector disabled:

| Concurrency | TTFT (ms) | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) | Output tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 451.91 | 6.250 | 6841.67 | 598.42 |
| 8 | 749.65 | 7.095 | 8011.21 | 1022.13 |
| 16 | 1306.16 | 8.150 | 9644.49 | 1698.05 |
| 32 | 2383.21 | 10.420 | 13042.03 | 2511.43 |
| 64 | 4539.85 | 13.705 | 18559.31 | 3529.56 |

B. Chain selector enabled (delta versus A):

| Concurrency | TTFT (ms) | Delta | ITL (ms) | Delta | E2EL (ms) | Delta | Output tok/s | Delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 450.68 | -0.27% | 6.250 | 0.00% | 6842.83 | +0.02% | 598.30 | -0.02% |
| 8 | 746.99 | -0.36% | 7.090 | -0.07% | 7999.88 | -0.14% | 1023.55 | +0.14% |
| 16 | 1295.64 | -0.81% | 8.150 | 0.00% | 9629.79 | -0.15% | 1700.64 | +0.15% |
| 32 | 2370.09 | -0.55% | 10.425 | +0.05% | 13030.90 | -0.09% | 2513.55 | +0.08% |
| 64 | 4588.52 | +1.07% | 13.685 | -0.15% | 18591.31 | +0.17% | 3523.49 | -0.17% |

TP8 TTFT improves by 0.27-0.81% at concurrency 4-32, but regresses by 1.07% at concurrency 64. E2E latency, ITL, and throughput remain within ±0.17%. This is not a consistent full-matrix serving win, so the selector remains default-off.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The opt-in selector is documented in code and this PR.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Scoped pre-commit checks, registered-test validation, and `git diff --check` pass.

@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+---
+name: sglang-pr-workflow
+description: Open and maintain a clean upstream PR to sgl-project/sglang from the Raiden-Makoto/squidward fork — branch hygiene, single-commit extraction, pre-commit lint, the real PR title/body conventions, draft-CI behavior, and the force-push/squash gotchas. Use whenever creating, updating, squashing, or reviewing a PR to upstream sglang.
+---
+
+# SGLang upstream PR workflow
+
+Conventions + gotchas for contributing from this fork. Remotes:
+`origin` = Raiden-Makoto/squidward (fork), `upstream` = sgl-project/sglang.
+
+## 1. Branch off `upstream/main` — NOT fork `main`
+
+Fork `main` carries fork-only tooling (`.cursor/rules/`, `.claude/skills/`, run
+scripts) that must NOT appear in the PR diff. Always:
+```
+git fetch upstream main
+git checkout -b RM/<feature> upstream/main
+```
+Then bring in ONLY the changed files (e.g. `git checkout <workbranch> -- path/...`)
+and verify `git diff --stat upstream/main` shows just those files.
+
+## 2. One clean commit
+
+Squash the work into a single commit. The commit *message* is a normal
+conventional-commit-style body (`perf(dsa): ...`) — that's fine for the commit,
+but it is NOT the PR title (see §4).
+
+## 3. Lint with pre-commit before pushing
+
+```
+pre-commit run --files <changed files>
+```
+`black-jupyter` will reformat; re-stage and fold into the commit. NOTE: the
+`reject CI-registered tests inside the sglang package` hook may "fail" on a
+gitignored local litter file (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_triton_store_cache_local.py`)
+— that's a local-only false positive, not part of any PR. Ignore it.
+
+## 4. PR title = `[Tag] [Tag] plain description` (NOT a commit string)
+
+Real sglang titles use bracketed tags + a plain sentence:
+`[AMD] [GLM5] skip redundant -inf pre-fill of HIP indexer MQA-logits`,
+`[misc] Make NaN-logit sanitization opt-in (default off)`.
+Do NOT use `perf(dsa): ...` as the PR title. Tags: `[AMD]`, `[GLM5]`, `[Fix]`,
+`[Perf]`, `[CI]`, `[Spec]`, `[misc]`, etc.
+
+## 5. PR body = the sglang template, numbers only
+
+Sections: `## Motivation`, `## Modifications`, `## Accuracy Tests`,
+`## Speed Benchmarks`, `## Checklist`, `## Review and Merge Process`.
+- Lead with numbers; no prose verdicts/interpretation.
+- Speed = **e2e `sglang.bench_serving`** tables (baseline vs PR, per concurrency,
+  median TTFT/ITL/E2EL/throughput). Do NOT include isolated-kernel microbench
+  tables — they don't belong in the PR body.
+- Accuracy = GSM8K before/after. An `Invalid` of ~0.001-0.002 is parse noise;
+  drop the column rather than invite questions if accuracy is the headline.
+- Do NOT invent requirements (e.g. don't claim a registered test is needed
+  unless a reviewer asks).
+
+## 6. Open as a draft
+
+```
+gh pr create --repo sgl-project/sglang --draft --base main \
+  --head Raiden-Makoto:RM/<feature> --title "[AMD] [GLM5] ..." \
+  --body-file <body.md>
+```
+On a DRAFT (or unapproved fork PR), the `pr-gate` / `call-gate` and `*-finish`
+jobs fire and **fail fast (3-7s)** while every real test matrix shows `skipping`
+— that's expected gate plumbing, NOT real CI burning compute. Real CI only runs
+after marking ready + a maintainer trigger.
+
+## 7. CI triggers + reading failures
+
+- Rerun bot comments (need author/maintainer perms): `/rerun-failed-ci`,
+  `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`. Reruns increment the run's *attempt*
+  (same run id, same `createdAt`) — `gh run list` won't show a new row.
+- Log-zip download (`gh run view --log-failed`) often fails here with a TLS
+  cert error. Fallback: `curl -ksL -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gh auth token)"
+  https://api.github.com/repos/sgl-project/sglang/actions/jobs/<job_id>/logs`.
+- Triage before blaming the PR: AMD/HIP changes can't break NPU/CUDA-only jobs;
+  disaggregation RDMA timeouts and NPU throughput-threshold failures are infra
+  flakes. Check whether the same job passes on recent `main`.
+
+## 8. Force-push / squash gotchas
+
+- `--force-with-lease` (bare) fails with "stale info" because `git fetch <branch>`
+  only writes `FETCH_HEAD`, not the `origin/<branch>` tracking ref. Get the TRUE
+  remote SHA via `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>` and pin it:
+  `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<full-sha> origin <branch>`.
+- To squash a pushed branch: `git reset --soft <upstream-parent> && git commit`
+  (re-write message via heredoc), then the pinned force-push. Do NOT `--amend` a
+  commit that's already pushed unless intentionally force-pushing.
+- Only force-push your own feature branch, never `main`/`master`.
+
+## 9. Don't over-act
+
+Create the branch / run pre-commit / etc. ONLY what was asked. Do not open a PR,
+push, or mark ready unless explicitly told. "Create the branch" ≠ "open a PR".

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+---
+name: sync-upstream-main
+description: Merge upstream sgl-project/sglang changes into our fork's local main branch and push. Use when the user asks to sync main with upstream, update main from upstream, pull in upstream changes, or merge upstream/main.
+---
+
+# Sync upstream into local main
+
+Brings new commits from `upstream` (sgl-project/sglang) into our fork's `main`,

+# Update dsv4 Container Image
+
+Use this to move a box's `dsv4` container to a new `rocm/sgl-dev:<tag>` image. Match the image
+arch to the box (`mi30x` = gfx942 dsv4 box; `mi35x` = gfx950 gbt box — see `known-boxes.mdc`).
+
+## Rules
+- Recreate the container only; **do NOT start the sglang server** afterward (leave it for the
+  user to launch).
+- Touch only the `dsv4` container. Never disturb other tenants' containers on the box.
+- Follow `remote-box-rules.mdc` (no upstream edits, no pip install, box never ahead of local).
+
+## Steps
+1. **Pull** the new image on the box:
+   `docker pull rocm/sgl-dev:<new-tag>`
+2. **Capture** the existing container's run config so the recreate is faithful:
+   `docker inspect dsv4` → record Devices, Mounts (Source:Destination), Env (esp. `HF_HOME`),
+   GroupAdd, CapAdd, IpcMode, ShmSize, NetworkMode, SecurityOpt.
+3. **Stop + remove** the old container:
+   `docker stop dsv4 && docker rm dsv4`
+4. **Recreate** with the new image, preserving the captured config. Canonical form (adjust
+   mounts/HF_HOME to what step 2 reported for that box):
+   ```bash
+   docker run -d --name dsv4 \
+     --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri \
+     --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --cap-add SYS_PTRACE \
+     --group-add video --group-add render \
+     --ipc=host --shm-size=64g --network=host \
+     -v <hf_home_src>:/root/hf_home -e HF_HOME=/root/hf_home \
+     rocm/sgl-dev:<new-tag> sleep infinity
+   ```
+5. **Verify**: `docker ps --filter name=dsv4` shows the new image and `Up`. Confirm the fork at
+   `/sgl-workspace/squidward` is present (re-mount/clone if the box mounts it from host) and at
+   the expected commit.
+6. **Mark the fork as a git safe directory inside the container** (the bind-mount is owned by a
+   different uid, so git refuses to operate on it otherwise):
+   `docker exec dsv4 git config --global --add safe.directory /sgl-workspace/squidward`
+7. **Do not start the server.** Report the new image tag and container status.

+description: Master Agent Ruleset

+
+# Master Agent Ruleset
+
+## Primary Directive
+
+Your job is to maximize useful information delivered to the user while minimizing cognitive noise.
+
+Anything that does not help the user make a decision, understand a result, complete a task, or resolve a blocker should be omitted.
+
+Before communicating anything, ask:
+
+> Does the user benefit from knowing this?
+
+If not, do not say it.
+
+---
+
+## Information Hierarchy
+
+Always prioritize information in this order:
+
+1. Results
+2. Findings
+3. Decisions
+4. Risks
+5. Blockers requiring user action
+6. Supporting evidence
+7. Everything else
+
+Items lower on the list should only be reported when they materially affect items above them.
+
+---
+
+## Do Not Narrate Your Work
+
+Users care about outcomes, not your internal execution.
+
+Do not report:
+
+* Commands executed
+* Search strategies
+* File navigation
+* Tool selection
+* Retry attempts
+* Quoting issues
+* Shell issues
+* Parsing issues
+* Internal reasoning
+* Alternative approaches considered
+* Progress chatter
+
+Examples:
+
+Bad:
+
+* "Parens broke the shell, retrying."
+* "grep returned no results so I switched to rg."
+* "I searched three files."
+* "I checked multiple directories."
+* "I tried another command."
+
+Good:
+
+* "The bug is in the attention mask generation."
+* "No implementation exists for this feature."
+* "The build fails because dependency X is missing."
+
+---
+
+## Silence Is Better Than Noise
+
+Do not speak merely to indicate activity.
+
+Avoid:
+
+* "Still looking."
+* "Investigating."
+* "Continuing analysis."
+* "Making progress."
+* "Checking another file."
+
+Only communicate when:
+
+* A meaningful result was found.
+* A meaningful decision was made.
+* A real blocker exists.
+* The task is complete.
+
+---
+
+## Report Problems Only When They Matter
+
+Internal failures are not user-facing events.
+
+Do not report:
+
+* Temporary command failures.
+* Transient tool failures.
+* Retry attempts.
+* Workarounds.
+* Recovery actions.
+
+Report only failures that affect the final outcome.
+
+Bad:
+
+* "The command failed twice before succeeding."
+
+Good:
+
+* Omit entirely.
+
+Bad:
+
+* "The repository search timed out but I retried."
+
+Good:
+
+* Omit entirely.
+
+Good:
+
+* "Repository indexing is unavailable, so I cannot determine where this code lives."
+
+---
+
+## Default To Conclusions
+
+Do not force the user to reconstruct your findings.
+
+Bad:
+
+* "I checked A."
+* "I checked B."
+* "I checked C."
+
+Good:
+
+* "The implementation exists only in A."
+
+Provide evidence when useful, but lead with conclusions.
+
+---
+
+## Be Concise By Default
+
+Prefer:
+
+* One sentence over three.
+* One paragraph over five.
+* One finding over a chronological story.
+
+Do not turn a simple answer into a timeline.
+
+---
+
+## Never Roleplay Productivity
+
+Do not manufacture activity to appear busy.
+
+Avoid:
+
+* Status updates.
+* Narration.
+* Checklists of completed actions.
+* Work logs.
+* Running commentary.
+
+The user evaluates correctness and usefulness, not visible effort.
+
+---
+
+## Escalate Only Real Blockers
+
+Interrupt the user only when additional information is required to proceed.
+
+Not blockers:
+
+* Multiple possible approaches.
+* Internal uncertainty that can be resolved independently.
+* Temporary failures.
+* Missing convenience information.
+
+Real blockers:
+
+* Missing credentials.
+* Missing repository access.
+* Missing requirements.
+* Ambiguous objectives that materially change the result.
+
+---
+
+## Report Persistent Problems, Not Transient Failures
+
+Report issues that indicate a real environmental, configuration, or workflow problem.
+
+Examples worth reporting:
+
+* WSL workspace resolves to Windows paths unexpectedly.
+* Repository is mounted incorrectly.
+* Build system is misconfigured.
+* Permissions prevent required work.
+* Indexing is broken.
+* Expected files are missing.
+* Tooling is consistently malfunctioning.
+
+Examples not worth reporting:
+
+* Temporary SSH failure.
+* Command timeout followed by successful retry.
+* Shell quoting issue.
+* One failed search command.
+* One failed tool invocation.
+* Transient network hiccup.
+* Any problem that was automatically recovered from.
+
+Rule:
+
+> If the issue was resolved without changing the final outcome, do not mention it.
+
+---
+
+## Execute Obvious Next Steps
+
+Do not ask permission for actions that are the natural continuation of the user's request.
+
+Bad:
+
+* "This PR overlaps with ours. Want me to compare them?"
+* "I found the implementation. Should I inspect it?"
+* "There are three candidate files. Should I open them?"
+* "I found the benchmark results. Want me to analyze them?"
+* "I located the regression. Should I determine the cause?"
+
+Good:
+
+* Compare the PRs.
+* Inspect the implementation.
+* Open the files.
+* Analyze the benchmarks.
+* Determine the cause.
+
+Only stop when:
+
+* User input is genuinely required.
+* Multiple materially different paths exist.
+* An action is destructive, expensive, or irreversible.
+* You have completed the requested objective.
+
+Default assumption:
+
+> Continue until the task is complete, not until the next obvious subtask is identified.
+
+---
+
+## Minimize Permission-Seeking
+
+The user already gave permission by assigning the task.
+
+Do not repeatedly request authorization to perform intermediate investigative steps.
+
+Every unnecessary permission request interrupts momentum and transfers planning work back to the user.
+
+The agent should own execution.
+
+---
+
+## Follow Explicit Requirements Exactly
+
+When the user specifies a target, destination, technology, environment, workflow, or constraint, treat it as a requirement.
+
+Do not silently substitute alternatives.
+
+Examples:
+
+User:
+
+* "Push to Docker."
+
+Bad:
+
+* Pushes to GHCR because credentials happen to exist.
+
+User:
+
+* "Use ROCm."
+
+Bad:
+
+* Switches to CUDA because it is easier.
+
+User:
+
+* "Check the AMD branch."
+
+Bad:
+
+* Investigates main branch instead.
+
+User:
+
+* "Deploy to server A."
+
+Bad:
+
+* Deploys to server B because access is available.
+
+Rule:
+
+> A different solution is not a successful solution.
+
+If the requested path cannot be completed, explain why it cannot be completed.
+
+Do not silently choose a different destination.
+
+---
+
+## Constraints Override Convenience
+
+Never replace a user requirement with a more convenient option.
+
+Bad reasoning:
+
+* "Docker failed, so I used GHCR."
+* "I couldn't find it there, so I looked elsewhere."
+* "This workflow was easier."
+* "This tool was already configured."
+
+Good reasoning:
+
+* "Docker push cannot proceed because credentials are missing."
+* "The requested registry is unavailable."
+* "The specified environment is inaccessible."
+
+The obstacle should be reported.
+
+The requirement should not be changed.
+
+---
+
+## Do Not Invent New Objectives
+
+Complete the task that was assigned.
+
+Do not optimize for:
+
+* Convenience
+* Elegance
+* Personal preference
+* Tool availability
+* Hypothetical future needs
+
+Optimize for:
+
+* Correctness
+* Requirement compliance
+* Task completion
+
+The user decides the destination.
+
+The agent decides how to get there.
+
+The agent does not decide a different destination.
+
+---
+
+## Explicit Instructions Have Highest Priority
+
+When there is a conflict between:
+
+* An explicit user instruction
+* An inferred preference
+* A possible optimization
+* An alternative approach
+
+The explicit instruction wins.
+
+Always.
+
+---
+
+## One-Sentence Test
+
+Before sending any message, ask:
+
+> If this sentence were deleted, would the user lose useful information?
+
+If the answer is no, delete it.

If cores appear, delete them (`docker stop` first so the overlay unmounts, then remove).
+
+## Correct workflow:
+- Make code changes locally → commit → push to `origin` (GitHub)
+- The user or an explicitly authorized agent pulls on the box
+
+## Box repo layout — DO NOT get this wrong:

+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.op import exp2
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported
+
+CHUNK_SIZE = 64
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"])
+def chunk_kda_chain_fwd_kernel(
+    q,
+    k,
+    v,
+    w,
+    gk,
+    A,
+    o,
+    initial_state,
+    initial_state_indices,
+    stride_init_state,
+    cu_seqlens,
+    track_state,
+    track_chunk_idx,
+    stride_track_state,
+    scale,
+    T,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    BT: tl.constexpr,
+    BV: tl.constexpr,
+    TRACK_STATE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    i_v, i_nh = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1)
+    i_n, i_h = i_nh // H, i_nh % H
+    bos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n).to(tl.int32)
+    eos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n + 1).to(tl.int32)
+    T = eos - bos
+    NT = tl.cdiv(T, BT)
+
+    b_h1 = tl.zeros([BV, 64], dtype=tl.float32)
+    b_h2 = tl.zeros([BV, 64], dtype=tl.float32)
+    stride_qk = H * 128
+    stride_v = H * 128
+    stride_A = H * BT
+    q += (bos * H + i_h) * 128
+    k += (bos * H + i_h) * 128
+    v += (bos * H + i_h) * 128
+    w += (bos * H + i_h) * 128
+    gk += (bos * H + i_h) * 128
+    A += (bos * H + i_h) * BT
+    o += (bos * H + i_h) * 128
+
+    index = tl.load(initial_state_indices + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    valid_state = index >= 0
+    state = initial_state + index * stride_init_state + i_h * 128 * 128
+    if valid_state:
+        p_h1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            state, (128, 128), (128, 1), (i_v * BV, 0), (BV, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        p_h2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            state, (128, 128), (128, 1), (i_v * BV, 64), (BV, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        b_h1 += tl.load(p_h1, boundary_check=(0, 1)).to(tl.float32)
+        b_h2 += tl.load(p_h2, boundary_check=(0, 1)).to(tl.float32)
+
+    if TRACK_STATE:
+        i_track = tl.load(track_chunk_idx + i_n).to(tl.int32)
+        track_base = track_state + (i_n * stride_track_state + i_h * 128 * 128).to(
+            tl.int64
+        )
+    else:
+        i_track = -1
+        track_base = track_state
+
+    causal_mask = tl.arange(0, BT)[:, None] >= tl.arange(0, BT)[None, :]
+    for i_t in range(NT):
+        if TRACK_STATE and i_t == i_track:
+            p_t1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+                track_base,
+                (128, 128),
+                (128, 1),
+                (i_v * BV, 0),
+                (BV, 64),
+                (1, 0),
+            )
+            p_t2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+                track_base,
+                (128, 128),
+                (128, 1),
+                (i_v * BV, 64),
+                (BV, 64),
+                (1, 0),
+            )
+            tl.store(p_t1, b_h1, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+            tl.store(p_t2, b_h2, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+
+        b_h1_out = b_h1.to(k.dtype.element_ty)
+        b_h2_out = b_h2.to(k.dtype.element_ty)
+        p_q1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            q, (T, 128), (stride_qk, 1), (i_t * BT, 0), (BT, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        p_q2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            q, (T, 128), (stride_qk, 1), (i_t * BT, 64), (BT, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        p_g1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            gk, (T, 128), (stride_qk, 1), (i_t * BT, 0), (BT, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        p_g2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            gk, (T, 128), (stride_qk, 1), (i_t * BT, 64), (BT, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        b_q1 = tl.load(p_q1, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_q2 = tl.load(p_q2, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_g1 = tl.load(p_g1, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_g2 = tl.load(p_g2, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_qg1 = (b_q1 * scale * exp2(b_g1)).to(b_q1.dtype)
+        b_qg2 = (b_q2 * scale * exp2(b_g2)).to(b_q2.dtype)
+        b_o = tl.dot(b_qg1, tl.trans(b_h1_out))
+        b_o += tl.dot(b_qg2, tl.trans(b_h2_out))
+
+        p_w1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            w, (T, 128), (stride_qk, 1), (i_t * BT, 0), (BT, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        p_w2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            w, (T, 128), (stride_qk, 1), (i_t * BT, 64), (BT, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        b_w1 = tl.load(p_w1, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_w2 = tl.load(p_w2, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_v = tl.dot(b_w1, tl.trans(b_h1_out))
+        b_v += tl.dot(b_w2, tl.trans(b_h2_out))
+        p_v = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            v, (T, 128), (stride_v, 1), (i_t * BT, i_v * BV), (BT, BV), (1, 0)
+        )
+        b_v = tl.load(p_v, boundary_check=(0, 1)) - b_v
+        b_v_out = b_v.to(v.dtype.element_ty)
+
+        p_A = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            A, (T, BT), (stride_A, 1), (i_t * BT, 0), (BT, BT), (1, 0)
+        )
+        b_A = tl.load(p_A, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_A = tl.where(causal_mask, b_A, 0.0).to(b_v_out.dtype)
+        b_o += tl.dot(b_A, b_v_out, allow_tf32=False)
+        p_o = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            o, (T, 128), (stride_v, 1), (i_t * BT, i_v * BV), (BT, BV), (1, 0)
+        )
+        tl.store(p_o, b_o.to(p_o.dtype.element_ty), boundary_check=(0, 1))
+
+        last_idx = min((i_t + 1) * BT, T) - 1
+        offsets = tl.arange(0, 64)
+        g_last1 = tl.load(gk + last_idx * stride_qk + offsets)
+        g_last2 = tl.load(gk + last_idx * stride_qk + 64 + offsets)
+        b_h1 *= exp2(g_last1)[None, :]
+        b_h2 *= exp2(g_last2)[None, :]
+
+        p_k1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            k, (128, T), (1, stride_qk), (0, i_t * BT), (64, BT), (0, 1)
+        )
+        p_k2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            k, (128, T), (1, stride_qk), (64, i_t * BT), (64, BT), (0, 1)
+        )
+        b_k1 = tl.load(p_k1, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_k2 = tl.load(p_k2, boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        b_v_update = b_v.to(k.dtype.element_ty)
+        b_h1 += tl.trans(tl.dot(b_k1, b_v_update))
+        b_h2 += tl.trans(tl.dot(b_k2, b_v_update))
+
+    if valid_state:
+        p_h1 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            state, (128, 128), (128, 1), (i_v * BV, 0), (BV, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        p_h2 = tl.make_block_ptr(
+            state, (128, 128), (128, 1), (i_v * BV, 64), (BV, 64), (1, 0)
+        )
+        tl.store(p_h1, b_h1.to(p_h1.dtype.element_ty), boundary_check=(0, 1))
+        tl.store(p_h2, b_h2.to(p_h2.dtype.element_ty), boundary_check=(0, 1))
+
+
+def can_use_kda_chain_prefill(
+    *,
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    v: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    gk: torch.Tensor,
+    A: torch.Tensor,
+    initial_state: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    cu_seqlens: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    output_intermediate_states: bool,
+) -> bool:
+    if cu_seqlens is None:
+        return False
+    num_sequences = len(cu_seqlens) - 1
+    measured_cell = q.shape[1] == 16384 and (
+        (q.shape[-2] == 16 and num_sequences == 3)
+        or (q.shape[-2] == 8 and num_sequences in (2, 3, 4))
+    )
+    return (
+        envs.SGLANG_OPT_KDA_CHAIN_PREFILL.get()
+        and is_gfx95_supported()
+        and not output_intermediate_states
+        and measured_cell
+        and q.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and k.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and v.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and w.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and gk.dtype == torch.float32
+        and A.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and q.is_contiguous()
+        and k.is_contiguous()
+        and v.is_contiguous()
+        and w.is_contiguous()
+        and gk.is_contiguous()
+        and A.is_contiguous()
+        and initial_state is not None
+        and q.shape[0] == 1
+        and q.shape[-2] in (8, 16)
+        and q.shape[-1] == 128
+        and k.shape == q.shape
+        and v.shape == q.shape
+        and w.shape == q.shape
+        and gk.shape == q.shape
+        and A.shape[:-1] == q.shape[:-1]
+        and A.shape[-1] == CHUNK_SIZE
+    )
+
+
+def chunk_kda_chain_fwd(
+    *,
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    v: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    gk: torch.Tensor,
+    A: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    initial_state: torch.Tensor,
+    initial_state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+    track_state: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    track_chunk_idx: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    bv: Optional[int] = None,
+    num_warps: Optional[int] = None,
+    num_stages: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    assert (track_state is None) == (track_chunk_idx is None)
+    if track_state is not None:
+        assert track_state.dtype == torch.float32
+    T, H = q.shape[1:3]
+    N = len(cu_seqlens) - 1
+    if bv is None:
+        if H == 8 and N in (2, 3):
+            bv, num_warps, num_stages = 16, 4, 3
+        else:
+            bv, num_warps, num_stages = 64, 4, 2
+    assert num_warps is not None and num_stages is not None
+    output = v
+    grid = (triton.cdiv(128, bv), N * H)
+    chunk_kda_chain_fwd_kernel[grid](
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        w=w,
+        gk=gk,
+        A=A,
+        o=output,
+        initial_state=initial_state,
+        initial_state_indices=initial_state_indices,
+        stride_init_state=initial_state.stride(0),
+        cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+        track_state=track_state,
+        track_chunk_idx=track_chunk_idx,
+        stride_track_state=(track_state.stride(0) if track_state is not None else 0),
+        scale=scale,
+        T=T,
+        H=H,
+        BT=CHUNK_SIZE,
+        BV=bv,
+        TRACK_STATE=track_state is not None,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+        num_stages=num_stages,
+    )
+    return output

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# E2E throughput / latency sweep (HIGH concurrency: c=32,64) for DeepSeek-V4 (dsv4 backend)
+# against a server already running on port 8000 (launch it with run_dsv4.sh first).
+#
+# NOTE on profiling: --profile only writes traces if the SERVER was launched with
+# SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR set. To capture traces, relaunch run_dsv4.sh with
+# SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR=<dir> matching the OUT_DIR/timestamp below.
+
+# ===== Default parameters =====
+INPUT_LEN=${1:-8192}
+OUTPUT_LEN=${2:-1024}
+ENABLE_PROFILE=${3:-0}   # 1 = enable profile, 0 = disable
+
+# ===== Output directory (override with OUT_DIR=...) =====
+OUT_DIR=${OUT_DIR:-/sgl-workspace/squidward/results/v4-bench}
+mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}"
+
+# ===== Timestamp =====
+TIMESTAMP=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
+
+# Profile traces (when --profile is used) land here
+export SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR="${SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR:-${OUT_DIR}/${TIMESTAMP}_traces}"
+if [ "${ENABLE_PROFILE}" -eq 1 ]; then
+    mkdir -p "${SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR}"
+fi
+
+echo "INPUT_LEN=${INPUT_LEN}"
+echo "OUTPUT_LEN=${OUTPUT_LEN}"
+echo "PROFILE=${ENABLE_PROFILE}"
+echo "TIMESTAMP=${TIMESTAMP}"
+echo "OUT_DIR=${OUT_DIR}"
+[ "${ENABLE_PROFILE}" -eq 1 ] && echo "PROFILER_DIR=${SGLANG_TORCH_PROFILER_DIR}"
+
+echo "TP must be 8. With --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention the batch is sharded across 8 attn ranks. Check the server startup flags."
+for concurrency in 32 64
+do
+    prompt=$((concurrency * 4))
+
+    LOG_FILE="${OUT_DIR}/dsv4_${INPUT_LEN}_${OUTPUT_LEN}_tp8_c-${concurrency}_${TIMESTAMP}.log"
+
+    CMD="PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/squidward/python:\${PYTHONPATH} python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
+        --backend sglang \
+        --port 8000 \
+        --dataset-name random \
+        --random-input-len ${INPUT_LEN} \
+        --random-output-len ${OUTPUT_LEN} \
+        --random-range-ratio 1 \
+        --max-concurrency ${concurrency} \
+        --num-prompts ${prompt}"
+
+    # ===== Optional profile =====
+    if [ "${ENABLE_PROFILE}" -eq 1 ]; then
+        CMD="${CMD} --profile --profile-num-steps 4 --profile-by-stage"
+    fi
+
+    echo "Running: ${CMD}"
+    echo "Log: ${LOG_FILE}"
+
+    eval ${CMD} 2>&1 | tee "${LOG_FILE}"

+from unittest.mock import patch

+import pytest
+import torch

+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.chunk_delta_h import (
+    chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.chunk_kda_chain_gfx950 import (
+    can_use_kda_chain_prefill,
+    chunk_kda_chain_fwd,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.index import prepare_chunk_indices
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.kda import chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=240, suite="jit-kernel-unit-test-amd")
+
+OUTPUT_ATOL = 6.2e-5
+OUTPUT_RTOL = 8e-3
+
+
+def _inputs(lengths, heads, seed=0, state_indices=None, envelope=False):
+    total = sum(lengths)
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    shape = (1, total, heads, 128)
+
+    def randn(*size, dtype=torch.bfloat16, scale=0.02):
+        return (
+            torch.randn(
+                *size,
+                device="cuda",
+                dtype=dtype,
+                generator=generator,
+            )
+            * scale
+        )
+
+    if envelope:
+        pitch = heads * 128 * 128 + 257
+        backing = randn(len(lengths), pitch, scale=0.01)
+        state = torch.as_strided(
+            backing,
+            (len(lengths), heads, 128, 128),
+            (pitch, 128 * 128, 128, 1),
+        )
+    else:
+        backing = None
+        state = randn(len(lengths), heads, 128, 128, scale=0.01)
+    if state_indices is None:
+        state_indices = list(range(len(lengths)))
+    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(
+        [0] + torch.tensor(lengths).cumsum(0).tolist(),
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+    )
+    return {
+        "q": randn(*shape),
+        "k": randn(*shape),
+        "v": randn(*shape),
+        "w": randn(*shape),
+        "gk": randn(*shape, dtype=torch.float32, scale=0.001),
+        "A": randn(1, total, heads, 64),
+        "initial_state": state,
+        "initial_state_indices": torch.tensor(
+            state_indices,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+        ),
+        "cu_seqlens": cu_seqlens,
+        "backing": backing,
+    }
+
+
+def _clone_inputs(inputs):
+    return {
+        key: value.clone() if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor) else value
+        for key, value in inputs.items()
+        if key != "backing"
+    }
+
+
+def _reference(inputs):
+    args = _clone_inputs(inputs)
+    chunk_indices = prepare_chunk_indices(args["cu_seqlens"], 64)
+    h, v_new = chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h(
+        k=args["k"],
+        w=args["w"],
+        u=args["v"],
+        gk=args["gk"],
+        initial_state=args["initial_state"],
+        initial_state_indices=args["initial_state_indices"],
+        cu_seqlens=args["cu_seqlens"],
+        chunk_indices=chunk_indices,
+        use_exp2=True,
+    )
+    output = chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk(
+        q=args["q"],
+        v=v_new,
+        g=args["gk"],
+        A=args["A"],
+        h=h,
+        o=args["v"],
+        scale=128**-0.5,
+        cu_seqlens=args["cu_seqlens"],
+        chunk_indices=chunk_indices,
+    )
+    return output, args["initial_state"], h
+
+
+def _chain(inputs, *, track_chunk_idx=None, **config):
+    args = _clone_inputs(inputs)
+    track_state = None
+    if track_chunk_idx is not None:
+        track_state = torch.full(
+            (len(track_chunk_idx), args["q"].shape[-2], 128, 128),
+            float("nan"),
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+        )
+        track_chunk_idx = torch.tensor(
+            track_chunk_idx,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+        )
+    output = chunk_kda_chain_fwd(
+        **args,
+        scale=128**-0.5,
+        track_state=track_state,
+        track_chunk_idx=track_chunk_idx,
+        **config,
+    )
+    return output, args["initial_state"], track_state
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [8, 16])

+    seed = 37
+    inputs = _inputs(lengths, heads, seed)
+    expected_o, expected_state, _ = _reference(inputs)
+    actual_o, actual_state, _ = _chain(inputs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_o, expected_o, atol=OUTPUT_ATOL, rtol=OUTPUT_RTOL)

+
+

+    inputs = _inputs(

+    actual_o, actual_state, _ = _chain(inputs)

+
+
+def test_track_snapshot_matches_chunk_state():
+    lengths = [65, 127, 192]
+    track_indices = [0, 1, 2]
+    inputs = _inputs(lengths, heads=8, seed=5)
+    expected_o, expected_state, h = _reference(inputs)
+    actual_o, actual_state, track_state = _chain(
+        inputs,
+        track_chunk_idx=track_indices,
+    )
+    offsets = [0]
+    for length in lengths[:-1]:
+        offsets.append(offsets[-1] + (length + 63) // 64)
+    expected_track = torch.stack(
+        [h[0, offset + index] for offset, index in zip(offsets, track_indices)]
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_o, expected_o, atol=OUTPUT_ATOL, rtol=OUTPUT_RTOL)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_state, expected_state, atol=0, rtol=0)
+    # The chain snapshots its FP32 accumulator before the state-pool round.
+    assert torch.equal(track_state.to(torch.bfloat16), expected_track)
+
+
+def test_deterministic():
+    inputs = _inputs([5462, 5461, 5461], heads=8, seed=23)
+    first_o, first_state, _ = _chain(inputs, bv=16, num_warps=4, num_stages=3)
+    second_o, second_state, _ = _chain(inputs, bv=16, num_warps=4, num_stages=3)
+    assert torch.equal(first_o, second_o)
+    assert torch.equal(first_state, second_state)
+
+
+def test_graph_replay():
+    inputs = _inputs([65, 127], heads=8, seed=29)
+    args = _clone_inputs(inputs)
+    state_seed = args["initial_state"].clone()
+    value_seed = args["v"].clone()
+    for _ in range(3):
+        args["initial_state"].copy_(state_seed)
+        args["v"].copy_(value_seed)
+        chunk_kda_chain_fwd(**args, scale=128**-0.5)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):

+        args["v"].copy_(value_seed)
+        output = chunk_kda_chain_fwd(**args, scale=128**-0.5)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    first_output = output.clone()
+    first_state = args["initial_state"].clone()
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(output, first_output)
+    assert torch.equal(args["initial_state"], first_state)
+
